key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over months to years. LOCATION: BILATERAL kidney involvement. DURATION: Chronic progressive condition. CHARACTER: PROGRESSIVE kidney function decline. AGGRAVATING: DEHYDRATION, medications. RELIEVING: DIALYSIS, medications, fluid management. TIMING: Chronic progressive, symptoms worsen over time. SEVERITY: 6-9/10, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: PROGRESSIVE KIDNEY FUNCTION DECLINE, swelling, fluid retention, may have nausea, vomiting, confusion, may have electrolyte imbalances. KEY POSITIVES: Progressive kidney function decline, swelling, fluid retention, elevated creatinine, elevated BUN. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

red_flags: Severe fluid overload with respiratory distress - possible pulmonary edema, call 911
Signs of severe electrolyte imbalances - confusion, seizures, cardiac arrhythmias - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of uremia - confusion, seizures, coma - call 911
Signs of severe metabolic acidosis - deep breathing, confusion, coma - call 911
